summary: Removed the two residual overstatements Director review found in the cumulative PR. In src/content/blog/beginner/life-line.md, the empirical-conclusion paragraph no longer says 'What rejects it is the evidence above'; it now states the mixed three-study evidence does not establish a reliable predictive relationship, and that Fincham, Gettings, and West (named earlier in the article) moved away from the lifespan reading, without claiming the evidence itself disproves or rejects the historical claim. The FAQ answer 'Does the life line predict how long I will live?' no longer says the 'modern practitioner literature ... rejects the lifespan mapping'; it now names the same modern sources and keeps the existing 'mixed record that does not establish a reliable relationship' wording. Both passages replaced anonymous 'modern practitioner literature' wording with the named sources. In src/content/lessons/lines/04-life-line.mdx, the sentence 'The modern literature broke with that' now reads 'Fincham, Gettings, and West broke with that', naming the same later sources the sentence already cites rather than implying comprehensive modern consensus. The verified three-study record (Wilson & Mather 1974, no correlation; Newrick, Affie & Corrall 1990, significant association; Lucas, Dhugga & Henneberg 2019, no correlation) and the historical Cheiro/Benham lifespan-reading facts are unchanged. Added Pass 10 to docs/source-verification-log.md and extended docs/CURRENT_STATE.md's PP-RELAY-024 note. No new studies, citations, historical claims, palmistry interpretations, or health/lifespan doctrine were introduced.
